cards.question: What is bhead-claude, and what does it do with a job board?
cards.answer: HR Scout: it scrapes job boards, has Claude extract structured postings, scores each one, and coaches interview prep.
cards.explanation: React 18 + Vite frontend, FastAPI + Motor backend, MongoDB 7, and the Anthropic API called directly with your own key. It began as an Understand Studio generated app; the `claude/standalone-app` line made it self-contained.
cards.anchor: A recruiting office conveyor belt: posters go in, a clerk types one index card per job, an examiner stamps a mark out of 100 on each card, a coach rehearses the candidate.
cards.evidence_quote: it scrapes job boards you configure, extracts structured postings with Claude, scores each extraction with deterministic quality rules

cards.question: Which invariant does bhead-claude exist to protect?
cards.answer: Every Claude call goes through ONE seam, `backend/app/llm.py`; nothing else imports `anthropic`.
cards.explanation: That makes swapping the model, adding a gateway `base_url`, caching or usage metering a one-file edit. Breaks if undone: an SDK call written inside a route escapes the refusal and truncation guards. The headless rail on `main` follows the same rule, see 61.
cards.anchor: A castle with a single drawbridge: every messenger to the oracle crosses it, so the guard there can change the toll or the road for all of them at once.
cards.confusables: `headless.py` on `main` — the seam of the other rail: the only place a `claude` SUBPROCESS is spawned, where `llm.py` is the only importer of `anthropic`.
cards.evidence_quote: Every Claude call in the codebase goes through this module; nothing else imports `anthropic`.

cards.question: bhead-claude: line `main` vs line `claude/standalone-app`: what is the ONE difference in how HR Scout reaches Claude?
cards.answer: `main` by default routes the SDK through Understand Studio's proxy with the per-app `UT_API_KEY`; `claude/standalone-app` calls `api.anthropic.com` DIRECTLY with your own `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
cards.explanation: `main` goes direct only in its opt-in standalone mode, see 82. `claude/standalone-app` is the freshest line. It also removed the bundled `claude-template/` scaffold, so the headless rail lives only on `main` (see 61).
cards.anchor: Two food stalls with the same recipe: one must buy every ingredient through the market owner's till, the other pays the farmer directly.
cards.confusables: `main` — by default needs the builder's runtime on the other end of every call; the standalone line needs ONLY your own key.
cards.evidence_quote: **AI calls** now go straight to `api.anthropic.com` with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

cards.question: bhead-claude · on the `main` line, one scheduled headless workflow: recite the 6 steps from the scheduler tick to the stored run record.
steps: `scheduler_loop()` wakes every 30 s -> finds an enabled workflow that `_is_due()`
`start_run()` -> returns None when the workflow id is already in `_active`
`update_workflow()` -> stamps `last_run` with the START time of the run
`asyncio.create_task(_execute())` -> the run continues in the background

cards.answer: `cp .env.example .env` (then set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), followed by `docker compose up --build`.
cards.explanation: Without the key the backend still starts; `/api/health` reports `llm.configured: false` and the first AI call fails with a clear message, see 32.

Great role
with a long enough text"}) # result.score ? result.band ? result.flagged ?

cards.question: Which module on bhead-claude's standalone line is the ONLY place a quality rule, band or flag threshold is defined?
cards.answer: `backend/app/quality/registry.py`: `RULES`, `BANDS`, `FLAG_THRESHOLD` as plain data; `engine.py` only interprets.
cards.explanation: Adding a check is adding a row. `validate_registry()` runs when the package is imported, and `GET /api/monitor/quality-config` serves the registry, so the UI never restates a threshold.

cards.question: bhead-claude: `_do_scrape()` vs `_do_scrape_apify()`: what is the ONE difference?
cards.answer: `_do_scrape()` FETCHES the page itself (`httpx`, then `_html_to_text()`); `_do_scrape_apify()` takes its text from the Apify jobup actor's items. Both end in the same `extract_structured()` call and schema.
cards.explanation: Caps follow the source: `scrape_page_chars` 12000 for the page, `apify_text_chars` 15000 for the actor items. The cron scheduler fires only `_do_scrape()`, so scheduled runs never spend Apify budget.

cards.question: Which function lets bhead-claude scrape cron-enabled targets with no manual trigger?
cards.answer: `scheduler_loop(db)` in `backend/app/scheduler.py`: an asyncio task started in the FastAPI lifespan, ticking every 60 s.
cards.explanation: Each tick selects active, cron-enabled, non-running targets whose `cron_next_run` is past or missing, reserves each one (`status` running, next run = now + `cron_interval_minutes`, default 1440) and fires `_do_scrape()` with `asyncio.create_task`. The tick is `SCHEDULER_TICK_SECONDS`.
cards.anchor: A lighthouse beam sweeping once a minute: every boat whose departure time has passed gets a BUSY lantern and is pushed off the quay.
cards.confusables: `workflows.scheduler_loop()` on `main` — same name, but it polls FILE-backed headless workflows, not Mongo targets.
cards.evidence_quote: asyncio.create_task(_do_scrape(db, tid, triggered_by="cron"))

cards.question: bhead-claude · `main` template: which Cloud Run deploy flag keeps a headless run alive after the 202 response?
cards.answer: `--no-cpu-throttling` — the run continues AFTER the response; throttled CPU would freeze it mid-run.
cards.explanation: `start_run()` returns at once and the CLI subprocess keeps working in a background task, which Cloud Run would otherwise starve of CPU once the response is sent.
cards.confusables: `--min-instances 1` — keeps the in-process SCHEDULER alive between requests; it does nothing for the CPU of a run already triggered.

cards.question: Why does bhead-claude's standalone line call `api.anthropic.com` directly rather than keep the generated app's Studio-proxy mode?
cards.answer: Outside Understand Studio the proxy host does not exist, so a proxy-mode call ends as a connection error; calling directly leaves ONE dependency, the owner's own `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
cards.explanation: `get_client()` now raises `LLMNotConfigured` when no credential is present. Breaks if undone: the app again needs the builder's proxy and per-app key to answer one request, and reports every call to the usage metering. The parent's dual-mode client is on `main`, see 81.
cards.anchor: Letters keep going to a mail room in a demolished building and come back 'address unknown'; the cure is to write straight to the recipient.
cards.confusables: `claude_examples.get_client()` on `main` — picks proxy OR direct from the environment; the standalone `llm.get_client()` has ONLY the direct path.
cards.evidence_quote: connection error to a host that no longer exists

cards.question: bhead-claude · the owner's question: why headless-bun-claude leverage Anthropic headless calls rather than plain SDK?
cards.answer: It does NOT replace the SDK: on `main`, `claude-template` ADDS a headless rail beside it. (1) `run_headless()` spawns `claude -p "<prompt>"`: the CLI's own agent loop reads files, greps and runs git in the mounted repo and accepts slash commands such as `/review`, a CLI concept. (2) The rule: SDK when your code knows the steps, headless when the model must discover them by exploring a filesystem; chat and extraction stay on `llm.py`. (3) `claude/standalone-app` removed the scaffold, so that line is SDK only.
cards.explanation: Breaks if undone: a repository review through the SDK means hand-writing the loop (the template's `chat_with_tools()`) plus your own file, grep and git tools, and slash commands are unavailable. On the headless rail, varying the workload is just varying a prompt string. Both rails read the same `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
cards.anchor: A librarian answering by phone must have every page read aloud to her; send the inspector INTO the library with a lamp and he finds the shelves himself.
cards.confusables: `chat_with_tools()` in the template's `llm.py` — an agent loop YOUR code drives over tools you write; `claude -p` runs the CLI's OWN loop with its built-in file tools.
cards.evidence_quote: Mode 1 when your code knows the steps; Mode 2 when the model must discover them by exploring a filesystem.

cards.question: Why does bhead-claude's standalone `extract_structured()` use `output_config.format` with a JSON schema rather than a forced tool call?
cards.answer: The API then guarantees that the first text block is valid JSON for the schema, so nothing has to be stripped or repaired; and the code records that forced `tool_choice` is rejected by current models.
cards.explanation: The parent version on `main` forced a named tool. Breaks if undone: per that code comment the extraction request is rejected by current models. `_strict_schema()` adds `additionalProperties: false` to every object node that does not set it, because the format requires it, and a test asserts that no `tools` or `tool_choice` is sent.
cards.anchor: A vending machine with a moulded slot: only a coin of the exact shape drops through, so nobody downstream has to sort the change.
cards.confusables: `tool_choice` with a named tool, in `claude_examples.extract_structured()` on `main` — there the JSON arrives as a TOOL INPUT; here it is the reply TEXT, parsed with `json.loads`.
cards.evidence_quote: (forced `tool_choice` is rejected by current models)

cards.question: bhead-claude: what stops a re-scrape of the same target from inserting a posting twice?
cards.answer: `_persist_jobs()` inserts ONLY when no posting of that target matches the title AND the company exactly, case-insensitively; a job with an empty title is skipped.
cards.explanation: State lives in MongoDB, collection `job_postings`. Title and company come from `extract_fields()` and are wrapped in `re.escape`, so a title such as `C++ Developer` cannot break the query. The check is per `target_id`: the same job found on two boards is stored twice.

cards.confusables: the unique index on `scrape_targets.url` — it blocks a duplicate TARGET in the database itself; postings have NO unique index, only this query.

cards.question: bhead-claude · `main` line (Understand Studio scaffold): how does the generated app's Anthropic SDK reach Claude in Studio mode?
cards.answer: `get_client()` builds `AsyncAnthropic(api_key=ut_key, base_url=base_url)`: the per-app `UT_API_KEY` is the bearer against Studio's Anthropic-compatible proxy at `UT_LLM_BASE_URL`.

Because the proxy is Anthropic-compatible, only the client constructor differs from a direct call (see 60). This deck is the home of that scaffold for the sibling generated apps.

cards.question: bhead-claude · `main` line (Studio scaffold): `increment_prompt()` vs `report_to_studio_counter()`: what is the ONE difference?
cards.answer: `increment_prompt()` reports a Claude call to BOTH Understand Tech's prompt quota and Studio's per-project counter; `report_to_studio_counter()` bumps ONLY Studio's counter.
cards.explanation: `claude_examples.py` calls `increment_prompt()` after every successful Claude call. Both are fail-open: a billing error never breaks a chat. The standalone line deleted the module, so nothing is metered there.
cards.anchor: Two turnstile clickers at a fairground gate: one clicks the park's tally AND the ride owner's tally, the other clicks the park's tally only.
cards.confusables: `report_to_studio_counter()` — meant for UT API v3 chats, which UT already counts server-side; calling `increment_prompt()` there would DOUBLE-bill.

cards.question: bhead-claude · `main` line: what does `_with_identity()` do to every system prompt of the generated app?
cards.answer: It prepends `_IDENTITY_PRELUDE` FIRST: asked who made it, the model must say it is powered by Understand Tech.
cards.explanation: The directive hides the underlying model and wins over any persona because it comes first. The standalone line removed it: a test asserts that the `system` value sent equals the caller's prompt exactly.
cards.confusables: standalone `llm.py` — passes the caller's `system_prompt` through UNCHANGED; nothing is prepended.
cards.evidence_quote: The directive comes FIRST so it takes precedence over any persona the caller layered on top.

cards.question: bhead-claude: you must make another Understand Studio generated app (same scaffold as the `main` line) run standalone. Following the `claude/standalone-app` translation, which host couplings do you cut?
cards.answer: Three groups; no data migration is needed. (1) AI rail: the proxy URL and per-app key, the usage-metering callbacks and the whitelabel identity instruction, replaced by one seam calling `api.anthropic.com` with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. (2) Host observability and branding: request analytics and error ring buffer with their `/api/__*` endpoints, the browser error reporter, badge and logo, the CORS wildcard. (3) Vault key: derive it from `SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY`; set it to the old per-app key to keep stored secrets readable.
cards.explanation: An empty `SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` disables the vault with 503 rather than encrypting with a guessable constant. `MONGO_DB` still defaults to `app`. This card is the portfolio home of the Studio scaffold: details in 81 (proxy), 83 (usage callbacks) and 84 (identity prelude).
cards.evidence_quote: The proxy URL, per-app key, usage-metering callbacks and the whitelabel identity instruction are gone.

cards.question: bhead-claude: which command proves the standalone backend works without a key, a network or MongoDB?
cards.answer: `cd backend && pytest` — the suite runs on a fake Motor database and a fake Anthropic client.
cards.explanation: `asyncio_mode = auto` in `pytest.ini`; the `api` fixture skips the lifespan, so no scheduler starts. On a live stack, `GET /api/health` shows `mongo`, `llm.configured`, the quality threshold and the caps before you spend a scrape.
cards.example: cd backend && pip install -r requirements-dev.txt && pytest  # no network, no Mongo
cards.evidence_quote: The LLM seam, exercised against a fake client — no network, no key.

cards.question: bhead-claude (standalone line): you add a field to `Settings` and put its variable in the repo-root `.env`, yet under docker compose the backend still runs on the default value. What did you miss?
cards.answer: The line in `docker-compose.yml`'s explicit `environment:` allowlist: a variable reaches the container ONLY if it is listed there, so the container silently runs on the default.
cards.explanation: A new setting needs three edits together: the `Settings` field, the compose allowlist line and a row in `.env.example`. Bare-metal `uvicorn` would have picked the value up, because `Settings` reads the repo-root `.env` itself, anchored on `__file__` rather than the working directory.
cards.evidence_quote: (otherwise the container silently runs on the default)

cards.question: bhead-claude: after a backend crash mid-scrape, a manual trigger answers 409 `Scrape already in progress for this target.` and cron never picks the target up again. What happened and what do you do?
cards.answer: The target document is stuck at `status: "running"`: a scrape leaves that state only through `_persist_jobs()` or `_mark_error()`, and neither ran. No route resets it, so set `status` back by hand in `scrape_targets`.
cards.explanation: The scheduler filters on `status != running` and both trigger routes return 409 on `running`. A `uvicorn --reload` in the middle of a scrape causes the same thing. It is an open item of the known drift; a reset route or a stale-run timeout would close it.
cards.evidence_quote: the scheduler skips it and manual triggers return 409. No route resets `status`.

cards.question: bhead-claude · `main` line: what happens to a tool call that would ask for approval during a headless `claude -p` run?
cards.answer: It is DENIED — print mode is non-interactive. Grant it per workflow with `allowed_tools` or `extra_args`.
cards.explanation: Read-oriented workflows such as `/review` work as they are; one that must edit files or run commands fails until granted, for example `allowed_tools=["Edit", "Bash(git diff:*)"]`. The module's rule: never default to bypassing permissions.
cards.evidence_quote: print mode is non-interactive, so tools that would normally prompt for approval are denied

cards.question: bhead-claude: what is the first open item to fix before HR Scout is exposed beyond localhost, and why?
cards.answer: Authentication: NO route has any. Whoever reaches port 8000 can trigger scrapes that spend Anthropic and Apify budget and can read vault secrets in plaintext through `GET /api/secrets/{name}/value`.
cards.explanation: Interim guard: keep it on localhost or put a reverse proxy with auth in front. It heads the known-drift list in `docs/SYSTEM_MAPS.md`, where the next pass starts; targets stuck in `running` (see 92) and non-atomic scheduler claims come next.
cards.evidence_quote: API behind a reverse proxy with auth before exposing it beyond localhost.
